input.quote: 4.3 Ownership of the Wet Segment shall be as shown in Schedule B to this Agreement. The Wet Segment of APCN 2 shall be owned by the Parties in common and undivided shares.
input.rationale: This is a consortium construction and maintenance agreement among carriers, not a vendor supply arrangement: there are no Deliverables, work product, feedback or Customer Data provisions anywhere in the document (searches for intellectual property, patent, copyright, licence, deliverables, work product and software return nothing). The only ownership regime is asset ownership in our favour — Terminal Parties own and provide their own Segments (4.1, p0107), the Wet Segment and Unallocated Capacity are held by the Parties in common and undivided shares in the investment proportions of Schedules B/C (4.3, 12.16), and we obtain Allocated Capacity on an ownership basis in return for our investment (12.2). IRU sales expressly convey no ownership (definition (i), p0054), so nothing transfers our title to another Party. Data and information is dealt with only as a mutual confidentiality obligation in Paragraph 31, which restricts disclosure rather than granting any Party rights in our information; there is no licence of our data to a counterparty and no processing right to narrow. Direction check: nothing assigns our IP or our data to the other APCN 2 Parties, and no counterparty owns anything we pay for without a corresponding interest for us. The undivided co-ownership of the Wet Segment is the core commercial bargain of a consortium cable (each Party investing for a proportionate interest and its own capacity), not the joint IP ownership the playbook targets, so we do not flag it. Noted only for the record, and not as a deviation: the Agreement contains no express IP/licence-back architecture, which is unremarkable for this document type given no Party creates deliverables for another.
